doc_screened_files.reason: Directly named in the ICE (`impossible case reached`) and the stack shows the panic in `Const::is_deterministic`; this is the immediate invariant site that GVN tripped over.
The crash happens while `GVN::insert_constant` / `simplify_operand` is running, so this is the direct trigger path that is classifying and reusing the problematic constant.
The program first reports E0080 for `<A<()> as Foo<()>>::BAR` before the ICE, so the constant-evaluation query layer that produced the erroneous constant is a strong upstream suspect.
This file owns the type-level constant representation feeding MIR lowering; an associated const like `T::BOO` passes through this pipeline before becoming the MIR constant GVN sees.
GVN shares the same constant-propagation space as this pass, so any bad constant classification or folding behavior here can surface in the optimizer path that later ICEs.
The failing program depends on lowering an associated const expression into MIR, and this file is the conversion point from THIR/typed expressions to MIR constants.

This file builds abstract constants and destructures evaluated constants; if the associated const is being represented or simplified incorrectly, this is an upstream place where that constant shape could go wrong.
It computes `type_of` for anonymous consts and const arguments from HIR context, which is part of the path that determines the type and shape of the const fed into later evaluation.
Generic-const and associated-const predicate collection happens here, so a missing or misapplied bound could affect how `<A<T> as Foo<T>>::BAR` is validated and later evaluated.
This MIR simplifier also rewrites constant-driven control and operand patterns, making it a plausible companion site if the same constant-form invariant is mishandled outside GVN.
